name: Zimmah
overview: Zimmah is a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as the son of Shimei. He is associated with the Gershonite branch of the Levites, descendants of Gershon, son of Levi. His role and identity are primarily recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:42.
namesAndTitles: The name Zimmah means "consider, plan" in Hebrew. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it reflects a meaningful concept within the biblical context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Zimmah as the son of Shimei. There is also an inferred relationship suggesting Ethan as his father, based on the same passage in 1 Chronicles 6:42. Beyond these, no additional family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Zimmah's significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogies, which are crucial for understanding the organization and heritage of the priestly tribe. As a Gershonite Levite, his lineage contributes to the broader biblical narrative of God's chosen people and their service. His mention in 1 Chronicles 6:42 helps preserve the record of Levitical families, underscoring the continuity of God's covenant through the tribe of Levi.
